entities.summary: Hermann Josef Giskes was a German intelligence officer of the Abwehr, the military intelligence department of the German military forces during World War II. He is best known for being the head of the counter-intelligence department of the Abwehr in the Netherlands from 1941 to 1944. He carried out an operation called Englandspiel or Operation North Pole which resulted in the capture of more than 50 agents of Britain's Special Operations Executive (SOE) and the confiscation of tons of military equipment, including weapons, which SOE had parachuted into the Netherlands to arm Dutch groups resisting the occupation of the Netherlands by Nazi Germany.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hermann Giskes' operation led to the capture of over 50 SOE agents and the confiscation of tons of military equipment, significantly disrupting British efforts in the Netherlands. This event had a regional impact on the war effort.
